GUIDELINES ON MANUFACTURE

A
AND TESTING

A-l.

During manufacture, a pair of opposite faces of block squares, for example A, and A,, can be `spot ground'* so as to achieve accurate parallelism between the opposite faces ( see Fig. 3 ). The accuracy of parallelism is checked by sliding the block square on a Grade 1 surface plate under a sensitive indicator.

SURFACE PLATE / 7777

FIG. 3

METHOD

OF TESTING

SQUARENESS

OF BLOCK

SQUARES

During the process of grinding the second pair of faces, B1 and B,, their squareness to faces A, and A,_is tested on a Grade 1 surface plate by means of a simple form of `squareness tester' ( see Fig. 3 1. Thus consists of a rigid angle block, the vertical arm of which is fitted with a transverse straight edge By this means, any out-of-squareness of face near the bottom and a sensitive indicator towards the top. Bt with respect to faces, Al and A, can be determined by taking the mean of readings on B, with the block standing first on AI and then on AZ. After correcting B1 for squareness 6, can readily be made parallel to 6,. It maybe mentioned that any indicator of the squareness tester.

EXPLANATORY
This standard was first published in 1968. current technical practices followed in India.

NOTE
First revision has been brought out in the light of the

The standard has been completely restructured in line with BS 939-1977 `Specification for ~engineers squares ( including cylindrical and block squares )`, published by the British Standards Institution (BSI). Dimensions and accuracy requirements are based on BS : 939-l 977 and guidelines on manufacture and testing have been given in Appendix A. 6 The Central Electric Press, Delhi-7
